text:
Maya: opened a small PR to tighten the dedicated provisioning migration doc and add a minimal autoscale SDK + terraform create example. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2528

Alex: skimmed. two quick asks: separate soft vs hard SLA guidance (don't mix percentiles) and fix a broken link I hit.

doc-linter: broken-link detected in docs/dedicated/migrate.md: line 42 -> https://docs.redwood.dev/dedicated/old-provisioning (404).

Sanjay: terraform snippet references reserved_pool_id but doesn't show creating the pool. can we add a one-line HCL to avoid confusion?

Maya: added HCL one-liner with isolation comment:
```hcl
resource "redwood_reserved_pool" "migration" {
  name = "migration-demo"
  gpu_count = 8
  # use isolation_label to segregate tenants
}
```

Lucy: switched the python snippet to use configure_autoscale (set_scale_policy is deprecated). example:
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient()
client.configure_autoscale(reserved_pool_id="rp-demo", target_utilization=0.75, min_replicas=1, max_replicas=6)
```
(added note: target_utilization is a fraction of GPU util, e.g., 0.75 == 75%)

Maya: replaced the broken link, added eviction_protection check to the migration checklist, pushed changes and requested reviews.

doc-linter: link-check passed.

deploy-bot: PR merged into main by Maya (https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/commit/c3d4e5f). Release note: "docs(dedicated): migration guide edits; autoscale SDK + terraform reserved_pool example; clarified SLA wording"

Maya: will follow up with console screenshot in a separate PR.
